fix.note: Founding privilege dated 20 March 1349 (old style), i.e. 1350.
Papal bull 1673 (Clement X); university created 1691, statutes sanctioned 1697, renamed Universitat Literària 1772. Suppressed 1829, revived 1840 and definitively suppressed August 1842.
Closed 1807 and restored 1814; incorporated into Alcalá in 1824 and definitively suppressed in 1837.

Closed definitively in 1902 (after this dataset's scope), hence end=null. Suppressed 1807 and 1842, reopened by the Carlists in 1874, and refounded as a Catholic university recognised in 1896; it began at Hernani (1542) before moving to Oñati in 1548.
Dominican higher studies date back to 1529; a royal decree of Philip IV (1645) created the university, so the c.1600 date is uncertain.

u-valladolid-1241-founding.note: The university says it was operating by the last quarter of the 13th century; exact origin unknown.

u-valladolid-1293-charter.note: The university dates Sancho IV's grant of the tercias to 1292.

u-lleida-1300-founding.note: Bull of Boniface VIII 1 April 1297; James II's privilege 1 September 1300.

fix.desc: The Avignon pope Clement VII confirms the university and its privileges (28 November 1379), adding medicine.

u-perpignan-1379-charter.note: Theology was not added in 1379: a faculty of theology was created by Nicholas V in 1447.

u-valladolid-1418-charter.note: The university dates Martin V's grant of theology to 1417.

u-girona-1446-founding.note: Privilege of 9 March 1446; papal confirmation only came in 1605.

u-barcelona-1450-founding.note: Royal privilege 3 September 1450; Nicholas V's bull later that month (suspended in November under pressure from Lleida).

u-huesca-1464-refoundation.note: One study dates the refoundation, backed by John II, the city, the Church and the Holy See, to 1465.

u-alcala-madrid-1499-founding.note: Bull 'Inter cetera', 13 April 1499; classes began 18 October 1508.

u-toledo-1520-founding.note: Bull of Leo X, 22 February 1520; the college itself was founded in 1485 under a bull of Innocent VIII.

u-santiago-1526-charter.note: Papal endorsements by Julius II (1504) and Clement VII (1526).

u-granada-1531-founding.note: Charles V's order 7 December 1526; bull 14 July 1531.

u-lisbon-coimbra-1537-relocation.note: The royal palace was bought for the university in 1597 and renamed Paço das Escolas.

u-zaragoza-1542-founding.note: Privilege 'Dum noster animus', Cortes of Monzón, 10 September 1542.

fix.desc: Julius III authorises the university founded by Bishop Álvarez de Acosta (bull dated 1 August 1550).

u-lisbon-coimbra-1555-confessional.note: Opened 1548 under André de Gouveia with masters from Bordeaux; taken over by the Jesuits in 1555.

fix.desc: The Estudi General begins to function on a stable footing in the building on the Rambla (built 1536–1539).

u-barcelona-1559-reform.note: The Rambla building dates from 1536–39; 1559 is when the studium began to operate securely.

fix.desc: João Delgado is appointed to teach the 'Aula da Esfera', now opened to lay students as well as Jesuits.

j-lisbon-santo-antao-1590-reform.note: The sphere class existed earlier for Jesuits; in 1590 it was opened to lay students under João Delgado.

u-tortosa-1600-founding.note: Enciclopèdia Catalana dates the university's creation to a decree of Philip IV in 1645, confirming a college approved by Philip II.

u-oviedo-1608-founding.note: Opened 21 September 1608; bull of Gregory XIII 1574.

u-mallorca-1673-charter.note: Clement X's bull gave its degrees universal validity.

fix.desc: Charles II sanctions the statutes of the Lullian University of Mallorca (created 1691; statutes published 1698).

u-mallorca-1692-charter.note: The university was created in 1691 and Charles II sanctioned its statutes in 1697; it was renamed Universitat Literària in 1772.

u-cervera-1717-founding.note: Statutes 1726; papal bull of Clement XII 1730.

u-lleida-1717-suppression.note: Closure ordered by royal decree of 9 October 1717.

u-tarragona-1717-suppression.note: The Literary Study was attached to Cervera in 1724 and closed in 1846.

t-barcelona-math-1720-founding.note: Created on the orders of the engineer-general Jorge Próspero de Verboom.

j-lisbon-santo-antao-1759-suppression.note: The Aula da Esfera ran from 1590 until the expulsion of 1759.

u-lisbon-coimbra-1759-confessional.note: All Jesuit establishments in Portugal were closed by force in 1759.

m-barcelona-surgery-1760-founding.note: Virgili named director on 19 September 1760; building opened 1764.

u-seville-1769-reform.note: Plan approved 1768, decreed 1769; move to the Casa Profesa on 21 December 1771.

u-lisbon-coimbra-1772-reform.note: The natural history museum and physics cabinet followed in 1773.

t-vergara-1776-founding.note: Installed in the former Jesuit college of Vergara.

t-madrid-veterinary-1792-founding.note: The faculty gives 1793, the year teaching began.

u-siguenza-1807-suppression.note: One account says the university was actually closed in 1807 and restored in 1814.

u-toledo-1807-suppression.note: A royal order of July 1807 listed Toledo for suppression, but it was soon found not to apply and the university kept functioning.

u-osuna-1807-suppression.note: Teaching continued until French troops occupied the building in 1810.

u-orihuela-1807-suppression.note: The 1807 reform cut its teaching to philosophy and theology rather than closing it.

u-irache-1807-suppression.note: Closure is given as either 1807 or 1824.

u-zaragoza-1809-destruction.note: The Paraninfo was blown up by French mines on 18 February 1809; repairs began in 1813.

u-salamanca-1812-destruction.note: Britannica dates the French destruction of the university quarter to the early 19th century.

u-valencia-1812-destruction.note: Much of the building, including the library, burned during Suchet's siege.

u-toledo-1814-refoundation.note: Re-established by royal cédula of September 1814.

u-osuna-1814-refoundation.note: No formal reopening is recorded; the university is said to have survived precariously after its 1807 suppression.

u-la-laguna-1817-founding.note: Decree of Ferdinand VII 1816; opened 12 January 1817 in the former Jesuit college.

t-caminos-madrid-1820-refoundation.note: The second school operated in 1821–1823 during the Liberal Triennium.

u-siguenza-1824-suppression.note: One account says it was incorporated into Alcalá in 1824 and definitively suppressed only in October 1837.

u-osuna-1824-suppression.note: It survived precariously after 1807 and was finally closed in 1824.

u-alcala-madrid-1836-relocation.note: A first short-lived Universidad Central was set up in Madrid in 1822.

u-lisbon-coimbra-1836-reform.note: The faculties of laws and canons were merged into a single faculty of law in 1836.

m-lisbon-medical-1836-reform.note: Reform under Passos Manuel; one account dates the medical-surgical schools' period from 1838.

m-porto-medical-1836-reform.note: Reform under Passos Manuel; one account dates the medical-surgical schools' period from 1838.

t-lisbon-polytechnic-1837-founding.note: Created from the Royal Naval Academy and the Royal College of Nobles.

u-osma-1841-suppression.note: A published study places the definitive suppression in 1840.

u-onati-1842-suppression.note: Decree of 11 November 1842 turned it into a secondary institute attached to Valladolid.

u-mallorca-1842-suppression.note: Suppressed by royal decree in 1829, revived as the Universitat Literària Balear in 1840, and definitively suppressed in August 1842.

m-cadiz-surgery-1843-reform.note: The royal colleges of surgery were dissolved by decree of 10 October 1843 and their masters passed to the faculties of medicine; Seville's medical studies moved to Cádiz in 1845.

u-huesca-1845-suppression.note: Huesca is not among the ten universities retained in 1845.

u-toledo-1845-suppression.note: Royal decree of 17 September 1845 turned it into a secondary institute.

u-salamanca-1845-reform.note: Salamanca's loss of doctoral rights follows from Madrid's monopoly on doctorates.

j-madrid-colegio-imperial-1845-reform.note: Became the Instituto San Isidro under the 1845 Pidal plan.

t-montes-1848-founding.note: Created 1846 on the Tharandt model by Agustín Pascual; first seat the castle of Villaviciosa de Odón.

t-barcelona-industrial-1851-founding.note: Inaugurated in 1851, taking over most of the Junta de Comerç's teaching.

t-agronomos-1855-founding.note: Created by royal decree of 1 September 1855; formal inauguration 28 September 1856.

t-segovia-1862-destruction.note: Fire of 6 March 1862; the college moved to the former convent of San Francisco.

u-salamanca-1868-reform.note: Theology faculties were suppressed in 1852, partly restored in 1854, and definitively abolished in 1868.

t-agronomos-1869-relocation.note: Suppressed in 1868 and refounded in Madrid in January 1869.

fix.desc: The province and city open a free university (inaugurated 14 November 1869).

u-murcia-1874-suppression.note: Ended by the law of 29 July 1874 suppressing the free universities, after years of budget shortfalls and low enrolment.

u-onati-1874-refoundation.note: The Carlist court re-established a faculty of theology; the course opened on 5 October 1874.

u-alcala-madrid-1882-access.note: Aleu and Castells received their doctorates about ten years after Maseras enrolled.

u-lisbon-coimbra-1891-access.note: Enrolled 1891; the source does not name her first course.

fix.desc: Reopened as a Catholic university, officially recognised as the Literary University of Oñate in 1896 and closed by royal decree in August 1902.

u-onati-1895-refoundation.note: Recognised by royal decree of 6 March 1896; closed by decree of 23 August 1902, not 1901.
